intended_object: An auxiliary relation between two two-step grid rectangle decompositions D, E of the same pair of grid states x, z. It records the side columns and intermediate state that the recut E must have when the two rectangles of D share their initial (left) side column. It is one of the four orientation cases used to build the recut involution that cancels the one-common-side terms of ∂⁻∘∂⁻ in grid homology (Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó §4.6). I inferred this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: This predicate is a proof device with no standard counterpart in the literature. It lists the side data (which columns are equal and which order condition holds) that the library computed for one orientation case of the recut construction. The module documentation lists it with three sibling predicates that are assembled into `IsRecut`, and from there into the involution `recut`. The mathematical content is the L-shaped-hexagon recut pairing of Ozsváth–Stipsicz–Szabó; this per-case table of side columns only serves to build it and to prove its properties (uniqueness, symmetry, involutivity). Mathlib has nothing comparable, so there is no generality question to assess.
